rows.text:
The first to fifth ionization energies (IE) of two p-block elements **X** and **Y** are given below.

| | \(\mathrm{IE_1}\) (eV) | \(\mathrm{IE_2}\) (eV) | \(\mathrm{IE_3}\) (eV) | \(\mathrm{IE_4}\) (eV) | \(\mathrm{IE_5}\) (eV) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **X** | 6.0 | 18.8 | 28.4 | 120.0 | 153.7 |
| **Y** | 8.2 | 16.3 | 33.5 | 45.1 | 166.7 |

The number of valence electrons in **X** and **Y** respectively are

Which of the following expressions represents the hydrogen atom wave function \(\psi(r)\) shown in the figure below?
(\(r\) is the distance of the electron from the nucleus and \(a_0\) is a constant)

figure.note: Plot of \(\psi(r)\) (vertical axis, ticks -0.2, 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8) against Radius, \(r/a_0\) (horizontal axis, ticks 0, 5, 10, 15). The curve starts near 0.7 at r = 0, falls steeply, crosses zero at about \(r/a_0 = 2\), reaches a shallow minimum of about -0.1 near \(r/a_0 = 4\) to 5, then rises slowly back towards zero from below by \(r/a_0 = 10\) to 15.

rows.text:
Which of the following molecules are aromatic?

**M**: pyridine; **N**: pyridinium ion, \(\mathrm{C_5H_5NH^+}\); **O**: pyrrole; **P**: pyrrole protonated on nitrogen, \(\mathrm{C_4H_4NH_2^+}\) (the ring N carries two H and a positive charge)

figure.note: Four structures labelled M, N, O, P: M pyridine (six-membered ring, three C=C/C=N double bonds, ring N); N pyridinium (same ring with N-H and a circled + on N); O pyrrole (five-membered ring, two C=C double bonds, N-H); P five-membered ring with two C=C double bonds and an N bearing two H atoms and a circled +.

rows._flag: The four molecules are drawn as structures only; their names/formulae are typed into the stem from the drawing (P is pyrrole with an NH2+ ring nitrogen).

rows.text:
Which of the following are aryl bromides?

**M**: 5-bromocyclopenta-1,3-diene; **N**: bromobenzene, \(\mathrm{C_6H_5Br}\); **O**: benzyl bromide, \(\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2Br}\); **P**: 4-bromophenol, \(\mathrm{4\text{-}BrC_6H_4OH}\)

figure.note: Four structures labelled M, N, O, P: M a cyclopentadiene ring with Br on the sp3 ring carbon; N benzene ring with Br; O benzene ring with CH2Br; P benzene ring with Br and OH para to each other.

rows._flag: The four bromides are drawn as structures only; their names are typed into the stem from the drawing.

rows.text:
An aqueous solution contains 1.0 M of \(\mathrm{X^{2+}}\) and 0.001 M of \(\mathrm{Y^{2+}}\) ions at \(25\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}\). \(\mathrm{X^{2+}}\) and \(\mathrm{Y^{2+}}\) ions do not interact with each other. This solution is put in an electrolytic cell and the voltage is gradually increased till a current begins to flow through the cell. The voltage is maintained at this point and a deposit is observed on the cathode. What is the composition of the material deposited on the cathode?
(Given: Atomic weight of X is 63 and Y is 200.
\(\mathrm{X^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow X}\), \(E^0 = 0.35\) V,
\(\mathrm{Y^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow Y}\), \(E^0 = 0.40\) V,
\(E^0\) is the standard reduction potential.)

For the reaction involving ideal gases, \(A(g) + 2B(g) \rightleftharpoons 2C(g) + 3D(g)\), which of the following plots is qualitatively correct? (\(K_p\) and \(K_c\) are the equilibrium constants in terms of pressure and concentration respectively. \(T\) is the absolute temperature.)
options: \(K_p/K_c\) against T: a curve starting at the origin and rising ever more steeply (concave upward)
\(K_p/K_c\) against T: a horizontal straight line at a constant positive value
\(K_p/K_c\) against T: a straight line falling from a positive intercept
\(K_p/K_c\) against T: a straight line rising from a positive intercept
